evals.prompt: Create a new skill for handling GraphQL subscriptions in a NestJS backend.
evals.expected_output: Follow the skill creation workflow: (1) Research NestJS WebSockets/PubSub practices. (2) Capture the outcome, trigger (*.resolver.ts, subscription, pubsub, websocket), expected output, acceptance criteria, scope, delegated choices, required evidence, and stop condition. (3) Classify hard invariants (evidence honesty, required gates) separately from method defaults. (4) Write SKILL.md using TEMPLATE.md — ≤100 lines, description ≤100 words. (5) Extract code blocks >10 lines to references/. (6) Create evals/evals.json with should-trigger and should-not-trigger cases.

evals.prompt: Audit this SKILL.md — it's 150 lines long with a 20-line code block in the body.
evals.expected_output: Quality violations: (1) SKILL.md >100 lines — extract content to references/. (2) Code block >10 lines — move to references/example.md. (3) Check description is ≤100 words with What+When structure. (4) Verify triggers are specific globs/keywords, not **/*. (5) Classify every rule before editing: retain hard invariants, adapt method defaults, move references. Fix each violation.

evals.prompt: The skill I created has low trigger accuracy — it only fires 40% of the time when it should.
evals.expected_output: Optimize description for trigger accuracy: (1) Add missing keywords to triggers list. (2) Add scenario-based phrases to description (what situations trigger this). (3) Run trigger eval queries. (4) Target ≥90% recall and specificity, matching the release readiness gate. (5) Spawn parallel subagents: with-skill vs without-skill (baseline). Grade assertions, iterate description until target met.

evals.prompt: Audit a project-local maintenance skill refocus. Its old non-slug name is replaced with a valid kebab-case name under .github/skills. The external installer scans agent skill directories and excludes metadata.internal: true; the public catalog must contain canonical registry skills only. The renamed local skill has no internal metadata and now appears as an extra installer entry. Keep the local maintenance role, but correct its distribution boundary.
evals.expected_output: Mark the repository-only maintenance skill metadata.internal: true so the installer excludes it. Preserve the valid name and canonical authoring references. Do not add it to the public registry expectation merely to silence discovery failure; verify actual installer discovery against the unchanged canonical catalog.
